name: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd
title: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd - 543248 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: India SSSG 12.6% on traffic with no price hike; gross margin 70.8% targeted to 72% in 3 years, capex discipline, but no capacity or supply-side metrics beyond 80 stores/yr pace and Indonesia capex on hold.

capex.quote: we are not looking at putting in capex to grow restaurants, but we'll find ways to bring in efficiencies at current ADSs

triggers.label: SSSG 12.6%, highest in 15 quarters
triggers.quote: Same-store sales growth was 12.6%. This is the highest we have done in the last 15 quarters.

triggers.label: No strategic price increase taken
triggers.quote: We haven't taken any strategic price increase at all.

triggers.label: Gross margin 70.8% toward 72% target
triggers.quote: Our goal is, as we have outlined in the last call, is to get to 72% over the next 3 years.

triggers.label: Popeyes strategic options under review
triggers.quote: we are looking at all options on Popeyes

guidance.quote: we would continue to grow at a pace of around 80 restaurants on an annual basis
Our plan is to get to 72% in the next 2 to 3 years.
If you bring that down to 5%, 5.5 %, 5%, then yes, the growth -- the EBITDA at the restaurant level will go up by that much amount.

we are slightly ahead of where we thought we would be in terms of gross margin

red_flags.label: Indonesia BK and Popeyes losses; Popeyes sale/hive-off under review
red_flags.quote: Popeyes, like I told you, we are now in very deep conversations with the new promoters.

evasions.quote: that is honestly completely the plan that the promoters have with respect to funding the acquisitions, honestly. So that's a question that rather we would kind of stay away from.
Once we have a steady plan put together that we are all fully energized and behind, then we will be in a position to share those plans.

summary.headline: India SSSG hit 12.6% in Q1 FY27 with revenue up 23.6% to INR682 crore and restaurant EBITDA of INR90 crore (13.2% margin).
summary.overview: Restaurant Brands Asia reported a strong Q1 FY27, led by India, where SSSG of 12.6% was driven by traffic rather than price, per management. India gross margin rose to 70.8% and company EBITDA more than doubled to INR52.7 crore. Indonesia remained loss-making at the Popeyes level but Burger King Indonesia reached positive restaurant EBITDA, with consolidated restaurant EBITDA of INR3.3 crore. A new promoter group has closed its stake acquisition, and management is working on a capital allocation plan for the next 3 to 5 years, with no details yet.

segments.name: Burger King India
segments.commentary: 590 restaurants (+71 YoY, +9 QoQ), 83% of group revenue; SSSG 12.6%, ADS INR1,31,000, gross margin 70.8%, restaurant EBITDA INR90 crore. Management targets around 80 net additions a year.

segments.name: Burger King Indonesia
segments.commentary: 137 restaurants (down from 179 after closing non-profitable units, per management), 15% of group revenue; ADS INR1,02,000, revenue INR124 crore, restaurant EBITDA INR6.4 crore. Bone-in chicken rose from about 30% to 50% of sales; self-ordering kiosks lifted average per check about 4-5%.

segments.name: Popeyes Indonesia
segments.commentary: 25 stores, 2% of group revenue; ADS about INR69,000, revenue INR15.7 crore, EBITDA loss INR3 crore. Management is in deep talks with new promoters and says strategic options, including exit, are not ruled out.

guidance_outlook: India gross margin target of 72% over the next 2-3 years (management said it is slightly ahead of plan at 70.8%).
India store growth pace of about 80 restaurants a year remains the goal.
Management said Q2 has started well, but it does not give forward guidance.
Indonesia: new value strategy expected to be in place by end-September; burger options in test in 3 markets since 1 July.
No new Indonesian restaurant builds planned this year; focus on rent reduction, solar, and a possible new broiler.
Franchisor RBI has committed USD9 million of marketing support to Indonesia over 3 years.
Management said a business plan and capital allocation plan for the next 3-5 years will come later; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: India expansion: 590 restaurants at 30 June 2026; target of about 80 net additions a year.
Indonesia: 137 Burger King and 25 Popeyes restaurants; portfolio cut by 42 restaurants over the past couple of years; no new builds planned in FY27.
Solar farm rollout across several India restaurants; new broiler installed that uses half the energy of the old one (management cited about 1-year payback in India).
Distribution clusters: management is building around distribution centres to lower primary and secondary transport costs.
demand_pricing: SSSG of 12.6% was traffic-led; management said no significant price increase was taken, only small price moves and some delivery changes.
Value strategy: 2-for-X offers (for example 2-for-99 and 2-for-79) remain the core of India's value positioning.
Premium and core menu: Korean and Peri-Peri burger promotions drove traffic; co-branded desserts and shakes contributed to growth.
Digital: about 90% of orders are digital; app and self-ordering kiosk data are to feed a CRM programme to launch soon.
Delivery profitability has improved; management said delivery mix rose on event-driven demand in some markets, not on competitor weakness.
Indonesia: the earlier 25,000 King Deal programme drove traffic but not enough volume; management said the 'missing link' is a new value strategy.
